## 1. Idea and references

**The idea in one sentence.** In the weeks when the weekly three-index switch (Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100 supertrends) is OUT **and** the weekly MAUc1 gold supertrend is SELL — the **OUT-SELL regime** — holding **Nifty 100 25%, Midcap 100 25%, Smallcap 100 25% and the liquid ETF 25%, whatever each index's own supertrend SIGN is** (variant `-all`), instead of the original sleeve, changes what the three-index switch earns: its CAGR and its worst fall; tried on both base sleeves (50/50 = T06/T11 Part A, 80/20 = T08/T11 Part B) on the two windows where the switch has been tested on the real parents, W2 now running to 2026-11-20.

**Where it came from.** Manu, chat 2026-11-26: "can you plan a T16. just the plan without the null, where in the out-sell weeks we will buy the Nifty 100, MC100, SC100 and Liquid ETF in equal weight ie. 25% each. its the same as the T15 but the buy conditions changes during the out sell weeks". Claude's reading (confirmed by his answers to `PLAN.md`'s decision points): T15's `-idx` held only the indices whose own SIGN was BUY, 1/(k+1) each; T16 drops that condition and holds all three, always 25% each with the liquid ETF. His answers: **D1** "(a) all six comparisons, C1–C6"; **D2** the eight T15 rules run as comparators and he asked that every rule and run be described in words on the page and in the md files (now a standing rule, AGENT.md R10 item 1, glossary in `AA/CLAUDE.md`); **D3** "(a) set 25% each on entry, then let the weights drift until the exit, obviously here exit mean we are out of OUT-SELL regime right?" (yes: the exit is the first decision that is IN or OUT-BUY); **D4** "window should be extended to the latest period till 20/11/2026 or beyond" and "data is approved to latest dates, please check" (checked: 2026-11-20 is the latest date every role reaches). His "lets execute T16" (chat 2026-11-26) approved `PLAN_v2.md`.

**The decision this will change.** What the book should hold in the OUT-SELL regime: the original sleeve (50/50 or 20% GOLDBEES / 80% cash), half parent + half GOLDBEES (T14 `-half`), the liquid ETF alone (T14 `-liq`), the liquid ETF plus the BUY indices (T15 `-idx`), or the liquid ETF plus all three indices (`-all`). The answer is **descriptive**: what each choice earned over the same weeks, prices and costs, as differences from the other holdings, with the spell-by-spell ledger. **No statement about chance or skill is made.** A pass of a comparison is at most PROVISIONAL: the variant was proposed after seeing the results of the original rule and of T14 and T15 on both windows.

**What is already known.**

| Ref | What it says | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| T06 / T08 / T11 (COMPLETE 2026-11-06 / 11-12 / 11-17) | The original sleeve: equity timing PASS on 2019-2026 (94-97 against random timing); all six criteria FAIL on 2014-2018, low power | `-orig` is this rule; **seen** |
| T14 (COMPLETE 2026-11-23) | The OUT-SELL regime held half parent + half GOLDBEES (`-half`) or 100% liquid (`-liq`): `-half` beat `-orig` in every book (+2.0 to +5.8 pp CAGR), `-liq` lowered CAGR in 16 of 16 book-windows | comparators; **seen** |
| **T15** (COMPLETE 2026-11-25) | The OUT-SELL regime held the liquid ETF plus the BUY indices, 1/(k+1) each (`-idx`): 4 of 16 comparisons pass, the windows disagree, `-idx` never beat `-half` (-6.0 to -3.0 pp), the W2 passes rest on one 10-week stretch (2021-01-29) | **T16's direct parent**: same regime, fourth holding. `-all` minus `-idx` measures what following the index signals inside the regime did, together with the weight change from 1/(k+1) to 1/4 |
| F-AA-M02 (T03) | A script that edits a document holding a frozen section must prove it did not change it | `fill_writeup.py` must leave §1–§3 byte-identical |

**What this test is NOT asking.**
- Whether holding the three indices beats **chance**, or whether the index signals pick well: no null is run (waiver).
- Whether any rule beats holding the parent (a comparator), or whether another weighting would do better. Ten rules, no search.
- Whether the variant has skill on weeks nobody has seen. There are none.
- Whether a real index fund or ETF would have earned what the price index did (§3, contaminants).
- Whether the best of the ten rules is the one to trade: picking it from these tables is a selection on seen data.
- Whether the rebuilt 2014-2018 parent NAV is the published one (none exists before 2019-01-02).
- **Which of its two differences from `-idx` matters:** holding the indices whose own SIGN is SELL, or the 1/4 weights in the weeks where an index is BUY. The ledger splits the weeks by k, but the test cannot separate the two causes.

## 2. Hypothesis and pre-registered comparisons

**Written before any run, 2026-11-26.** What was already known:
- **Both windows are seen, and so are T14's and T15's results.** `-liq` lost CAGR in every book-window (T14); `-idx` lost to `-orig` and `-liq` on W1, gained +0.7 to +0.8 pp over `-liq` on W2 almost entirely from the 2021-01-29 stretch (Midcap 100 + Smallcap 100, 10 weeks), and never beat `-half` (T15). The ledgers of both tests (what the parent, GOLDBEES, cash and each index returned in each spell) were seen. **The variant was proposed after seeing all of this**: any finding is **PROVISIONAL at most**, and there is no hold-out. The three new W2 weeks (2026-11-06 → 11-20) were in no test, but they are not unseen: they happened before the request and their signals are in the approved-data notes; they are three weeks of one spell, so they cannot serve as a hold-out.
- **No null is run** (waiver). **No statement about chance or skill can be made.**
- **The regime was counted before this section was written** (`spell_counts.py`, `logs/step_1_spell_counts.json`; signals, calendars and basket dates only; no price, NAV or return). **W1** (D26 calendar, T15's inputs): 1,070 sessions, 228 weekly decisions, first state IN; IN 93, OUT-BUY 81, OUT-SELL 54 weeks in 8 spells (7, 6, 7, 1, 11, 11, 9, 2); in the OUT-SELL weeks **k = 0 in 21, k = 1 in 18, k = 2 in 15**; so `-all` holds the three indices in **54 weeks, in all 8 spells** (T15's `-idx`: 33 in 6); B changes inside OUT-SELL 8 (T15 traded each; `-all` trades none). **W2** (D17 calendar of `extended_2026-11-25`, cut at 2026-11-20): 1,946 sessions (SCMO_0007 1,944), 413 decisions (412), first state OUT-BUY; IN 201, OUT-BUY 163, OUT-SELL 49 weeks in 8 spells (1, 4, 10, 2, 12, 11, 4, 5); **k = 0 in 24, k = 1 in 3, k = 2 in 22**; `-all` holds the indices in **49 weeks, in all 8 spells** (`-idx`: 25 in 7); B changes 8. **The three new weeks** (SIGNs as in the data: Nifty 100 / Midcap 100 / Smallcap 100 / MAUc1) 2026-11-06 BUY / SELL / SELL / SELL; 2026-11-13 BUY / BUY / SELL / SELL; 2026-11-20 BUY / BUY / SELL / SELL: the switch stays OUT and gold SELL, so **W2's last OUT-SELL spell runs 2026-10-23 → 2026-11-20 (5 weeks instead of 2)**; it ends at the window end, the last decision (11-20) is made, not traded, and the open position is marked at the 2026-11-20 closes. Trades from regime and gold changes (`-all` equals `-liq` by construction): W1 15 (`50-orig`) / 24 / 24 / **24** (`-all`) / 32 (`-idx`); W2 18 / 27 / 27 / **27** / 35. R3 windows: W1 from 2015-01-02: 44 OUT-SELL weeks in 7 spells, 21 trades; W2 live from 2021-11-01: 34 OUT-SELL weeks in 5 spells, 16 trades. (The plan quoted 1,947 W2 sessions; the count is 1,946, and the count wins.)
- **The effective sample is the 8 OUT-SELL spells per window** (7 and 5 in the R3 windows); the four books are one market seen four times.
- **Settled by Manu, 2026-11-26:** **D1** what is judged: the six descriptive comparisons C1-C6 below, pass mark 3 of 4 books (the D-table and the ledger are printed in any case); **D2** the eight T15 rules (`-orig`, `-liq`, `-half`, `-idx` on both bases) are re-run by the same engine as comparators and as the regression gate against T15's stored NAVs; **D3** `-all` is set to 25% each on entry and left to drift until the book leaves OUT-SELL, no weekly reset (so no R6); **D4** W2 is extended to 2026-11-20, the latest date every role reaches, W1 unchanged. A change after the freeze is a revision beside this file, never an edit.
- **Expectation, declared, no direction claimed.** `-all` puts 75% of the book in equities in every OUT-SELL week, against `-idx`'s 0-67% and `-liq`'s 0%, so it is closer to "stay invested" than any earlier variant except `-half`. Its difference from `-idx` has two parts that this test **cannot separate**: holding the indices whose own signal is SELL (the 21 / 24 k = 0 weeks are this alone) and the weight change from 1/(k+1) to 1/4 in the k ≥ 1 weeks. The ledger splits the difference by k so the reader sees where it comes from. Since the switch is OUT in every OUT-SELL week, at least one index `-all` holds is on its own SELL in every such week, and all three are in the k = 0 weeks.

### 2.0 The rules and the runs in plain words (standing rule, AGENT.md R10 item 1)

**States, read every Friday and on T0:** **IN** = Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 weekly supertrend SIGNs all BUY, the book holds the parent's basket. Otherwise the switch is **OUT** and the book holds a *sleeve*: **OUT-BUY** = OUT and the weekly MAUc1 gold SIGN is BUY; **OUT-SELL** = OUT and MAUc1 is SELL. **B** = the indices whose own SIGN is BUY in an OUT week, **k** = how many (0, 1 or 2). **Base sleeve**: **50** = 50% GOLDBEES / 50% cash in both OUT states; **80** = 80% GOLDBEES / 20% cash when gold is BUY and 20% / 80% when gold is SELL. Cash = the LBES liquid-ETF level. The ten rules differ only in what they hold in OUT-SELL (§2.1).

| Run label | What it is in words | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **W1** | 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02, the parent rebuilt from its baskets and stock prices (no published NAV exists), 228 weekly decisions | window; T11's / T14's / T15's inputs, pinned |
| **W2** | 2019-01-02 (SCMO_0007: 2019-01-04) → **2026-11-20**, calendar of the published NAVs, 413 weekly decisions | window; T08's inputs, **extended** from T15's 2026-10-30 |
| **live** (R3, W2) | W2's decisions from 2021-11-01, the AA books' live period | robustness |
| **R1** | round-trip cost 0 and 50 bps instead of 20.8 | robustness |
| **R2** | LIQUIDCASE as the cash leg (W1 whole window; W2 from 2024-01-24) | robustness |
| **R3** | a later start: W1 from 2015-01-02, W2 from 2021-11-01, each with its own first state (both start in OUT-SELL) | robustness |
| **R4** | leave one OUT-SELL spell out: `-all` holds 100% cash in that spell only | robustness |
| **R5** | a fund-cost drag of 0.5 pp a year on each index leg | robustness |

### 2.1 The ten rules

Regimes are read at each weekly decision. A target is the book's split across parent / GOLDBEES / cash / Nifty 100 / Midcap 100 / Smallcap 100.

| Rule id | Base | IN | OUT-BUY | **OUT-SELL** | Role and origin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `50-orig` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | comparator, regression; T06 / T11 A |
| `50-liq` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | cash 1 | comparator, regression; T14 |
| `50-half` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | parent 0.5, GOLDBEES 0.5 | comparator, regression; T14 |
| `50-idx` | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | cash and each index in B, 1/(k+1) each | comparator, regression; T15 |
| **`50-all`** | 50/50 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5 | **cash 0.25, Nifty 100 0.25, Midcap 100 0.25, Smallcap 100 0.25** | **new** |
| `80-orig` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | GOLDBEES 0.2, cash 0.8 | comparator, regression; T08 / T11 B |
| `80-liq` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | cash 1 | comparator, regression; T14 |
| `80-half` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | parent 0.5, GOLDBEES 0.5 | comparator, regression; T14 |
| `80-idx` | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | cash and each index in B, 1/(k+1) each | comparator, regression; T15 |
| **`80-all`** | 80/20 | parent 1 | GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2 | **cash 0.25, Nifty 100 0.25, Midcap 100 0.25, Smallcap 100 0.25** | **new** |

`-all` holds no parent and no GOLDBEES in the regime, and 75% in the three indices. **Change one thing at a time:** the only change from T15's rules is the OUT-SELL target of the two new rules; the eight T15 rules are unchanged.

### 2.2 Execution of the new states

Everything not listed is T15 §2.2 / T14 §3 unchanged (decide on the last session of each ISO week and T0; read the latest D03 and MAUc1 rows dated on or before the decision; trade on the next session at OHLC4; 10.4 bps a side on every value traded, 20.8 bps round trip primary, 0 and 50 as robustness; initial position free; the last decision is made, not traded).

1. **When a trade happens.** On the session after decision j iff decision j's target differs from decision j−1's. For `-all` the OUT-SELL target is fixed, so **only entries into and exits from the regime trade**; a change of an index SIGN inside the regime does **not** trade (the opposite of `-idx`).
2. **What a trade does.** T15's `trade()` unchanged: at the session's fill prices (stocks OHLC4, GOLDBEES de-spiked OHLC4, cash at its level, each index at its own OHLC4), V = value of all holdings; target value of each line = target share × V; traded = Σ|target − held| over every line; cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 1e4; every target is scaled by (V − cost) ÷ V.
3. **No reset inside the regime (D3 = a).** The four lines are set to 25% on entry and then drift until the exit; nothing is traded weekly. **The exit is the first decision that is not OUT-SELL**: IN (back to the parent) or OUT-BUY (MAUc1 turns BUY: to the base sleeve); the trade is on the next session.
4. **Parent rebalances while `-all` is in OUT-SELL:** the parent share is 0, nothing is traded. The `-half` comparators keep T14's D1 rule.
5. **Index marking and missing bars:** units × the index close. On a calendar session with no index bar (W2: the Budget weekend sessions 2020-02-01, 2025-02-01, 2026-02-01, all last sessions of their ISO week, so decision sessions, never trade sessions) the last close is carried and counted in `audit.json`. If a trade session ever lacks an index bar, the engine stops.
6. **Same-session collisions** (as T15): a basket change on the session of a regime trade is one trade to the new basket at the new target; a gold flip and an exit on the same decision is one trade straight to the new target.

### 2.3 The pre-registered comparisons (descriptive; no null)

For each window w in {W1, W2} and base b in {50, 80}, judged per book after 20.8 bps over the whole window:

| # | Statement about `b-all` | Comparator | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | earns more than the original rule | `b-orig` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C2 | its worst fall is no deeper than the original's | `b-orig` | maximum drawdown shallower or equal in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C3 | holding the three indices adds to holding only cash in the regime | `b-liq` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C4 | does better than holding half the parent and half GOLDBEES in the regime | `b-half` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C5 | ignoring the index signals in the regime earns more than following them | `b-idx` | CAGR higher in ≥ 3 of 4 books |
| C6 | ignoring them does not deepen the worst fall | `b-idx` | maximum drawdown shallower or equal in ≥ 3 of 4 books |

**24 comparisons** (6 × 2 bases × 2 windows). "Higher" and "shallower or equal" are by the unrounded statistics. Printed beside each: the difference in pp per book, Calmar, volatility, trades and cost paid. **The four books are one market seen four times**, and in OUT-SELL weeks `-all` holds exactly the same four lines in every book, so "3 of 4" is close to automatic for the regime part; **a pass is a description of seen weeks, never a claim about chance.** Choosing the best of the ten rules from these tables is a selection on seen data, and the write-up says so. No multiplicity adjustment is made (nothing is tested against chance).

### 2.4 The headline the decision needs (descriptive)

- **Rules and runs table** first (§2.0 and §2.1 restated in words on the page, AGENT.md R10 item 1).
- **D-table:** per window, book and cost: CAGR, maximum drawdown, Calmar, volatility of all ten rules, and the differences `-all` − `-orig`, − `-liq`, − `-half`, − `-idx`; start and end dates; trades and cost; weeks and sessions in each regime and in each k.
- **Regime ledger:** for each OUT-SELL spell and each B stretch inside it (so by k): dates, weeks, B, the return of each index, cash, GOLDBEES and the parent over the stretch (first fill to last fill), and each rule's return over it; **`-all` − `-idx` summed separately over the k = 0 weeks and the k ≥ 1 weeks.**
- **Comparators** (benchmarks): hold the parent; hold each index alone over the window; the equal-weight three-index basket alone; the **constant mix** at `-all`'s own average shares of parent, GOLDBEES, cash and each index (mean over the weekly decisions of the rule's target shares), rebalanced at every decision.

### 2.5 Outcome map (frozen)

| Pattern (per window, per base) | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| C1 and C3 pass | holding the three indices with cash earned more than the original sleeve and more than cash alone on this window; PROVISIONAL (seen, post-hoc, no null) |
| C3 passes, C1 fails | the indices beat cash but giving up GOLDBEES cost more than they added |
| C3 fails | holding the three indices did not beat cash in the regime on this window |
| C5 passes / fails | ignoring the index signals in the regime earned more / less than following them (T15) on this window; the ledger's k = 0 / k ≥ 1 split says where |
| C6 fails | ignoring the signals deepened the worst fall against T15 |
| C4 passes / fails | `-all` did better / worse than T14's `-half` on this window |
| R4 flips a passing comparison when one spell is left out | the result rests on that spell; say which; at most a description of it |
| the two windows disagree | report both; no general statement; the 2019-2026 window is the one the live product traded |
| R3 (live) disagrees with the full window | reported in the verdict and status note |
| a V gate fails | nothing is read; fix; new run directory |

### 2.6 Validity gates (any failure: nothing below may be read)

| # | Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Independent verifier `analysis/verify_t16.py`, written by a **different agent** from the engine's, from `logs/verifier_spec.md`, never opening `t16_engine.py` (it may read `verify_t15.py`) | Imports nothing from the engine, `approved_data.py` or any AA analysis module; parses `APPROVED_DATA.md` itself; checks every input is APPROVED with matching sha256 and a through-date covering the window. Re-derives from the raw files, per window: the decisions, regimes and B; the ten rules' NAVs at every cost and R1-R5 variant; every trade. End NAV within relative 1e-9, daily NAV within 1e-9. Exits 0 only if rows were compared and none failed; corrupted copies must exit non-zero (a `-all` regime week at 1/3 or without one index, an index SIGN change traded inside the regime, GOLDBEES held in a `-all` regime week, a NAV scaled, a trade removed, an index price shifted by one session) |
| V2 | Point in time | every decision reads Master and MAUc1 rows dated on or before it; every trade is on a later session; counted; violations 0 of a count > 0 |
| V3 | Index data tie | at every weekly decision of both windows, D03's `Index` column equals the index close of D25 / D25d on that date for all three indices; every trade session has a bar for each index |
| V4 | Regression and identities | (a) the eight T15 rules reproduce T15's stored `daily_nav.csv` and `trades.csv` to relative 1e-12: W1 on every session; **W2 on every session 2019-01-02 → 2026-10-30 and every trade on or before 2026-10-30** (T15's last W2 decision was not traded, so later trades are new); every book, cost and rule; (b) with every index price replaced by the cash level and cost 0, `-all` equals `-liq` to 1e-12; (c) `-all` equals `-liq` on every session before the first regime entry; (d) automated diff of shared functions against `t15_engine.py` lists only the expected changes; (e) the signals equal the SIGN columns of D03, D24c (W2), D24b (W1), and on W2 to 2026-10-30 equal T15's stored `decisions.csv`; (f) T15's one-instrument identity |
| V5 | Trade and cost identities | after every `-all` regime entry each index and cash = 0.25 of the value after cost, parent and GOLDBEES 0, to 1e-12 of NAV; index units constant through every spell (no trade on an index SIGN change); index units 0 outside OUT-SELL; cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 1e4; one entry and one exit worked by hand in §4.0a |

Oracle, negative-control and planted-effect controls (N6.7) are **not run**; they are untested (§6).

### 2.7 Robustness (reported; they set a finding's status, not the comparisons)

- **R1:** C1-C6 and the D-table at 0 and 50 bps.
- **R2:** C1-C6 and the D-table with LIQUIDCASE as the cash leg (W1 the whole window; W2 from 2024-01-24, as T08/T14/T15). Cash is a quarter of `-all`'s regime holding.
- **R3:** C1-C6 and the D-table on W1 from 2015-01-02 and on W2's live decisions from 2021-11-01 (each with its own first state; both start in OUT-SELL, so `-all` starts at 25% each at that day's closes, free).
- **R4: leave one spell out.** For each OUT-SELL spell s, a run in which `-all` holds `-liq`'s target (100% cash) during spell s only; C1-C6 recomputed. Shows whether one spell (in W2, 2021-01-29 or the last spell, 2026-10-23 → 11-20) carries the verdict. Deterministic.
- **R5: fund-cost drag on the index leg.** C1-C6 with every index OHLC4 and close of session i multiplied by (1 − 0.005 ÷ 252)^i, i counted in sessions of the window's calendar from T0 (as T15). The opposite side, dividends, is **not run**: no approved dividend series exists; disclosed as untested.
- (No R6, the weekly reset: D3 = a.)

## 3. Methodology

**Data.** Every file is a row of `data/APPROVED_DATA.md` (status APPROVED) and is opened only through the approved-data check; the engine writes `inputs.csv` (path, through-date, bytes, sha256, approved row, usable-from) from those rows and stops on a sha256 mismatch or a read before a usable-from date. **W1 uses exactly T15's W1 inputs** (same files, same sha256); **W2 uses the extended files below**, and every extended file holds the rows T15 read verbatim (registry notes: D17 and D11 verbatim tails / byte prefixes, D18 append mode, D25d equal to D25c, D03 equal on every used column, D24c equal to D24b), so the eight T15 rules must reproduce T15's stored W2 results on every session to 2026-10-30 (gate V4(a)).

| | **W1** (T11's / T14's / T15's window) | **W2** (T08's window, extended) |
|---|---|---|
| Dates | 2014-09-01 → 2019-01-02 | 2019-01-02 (SCMO_0007: 2019-01-04) → **2026-11-20** (the last decision, made, not traded) |
| Calendar | D26 NSE sessions (`index_daily_pre2019/nse_trading_days.csv`, 1,070 sessions) | D17 dates of `Historical Data/extended_2026-11-25/published_nav/SCMO_<p>.csv`, cut at 2026-11-20 (1,946 sessions; SCMO_0007 1,944) |
| Stock OHLC (D18), Polyplex correction (F-AA-D14), basket weights (D19), skips and dates (D05) | `data/holdings_matrix/SCMO_<p>_ohlc.csv`, `price_corrections.csv`, `*_holding_weight_matrix.csv`, `_columns.csv`, `_holding_weight_sources.csv`; `Historical Data/frozen_2026-09-25/Rebalance_history/` | `Historical Data/extended_2026-11-25/holdings_ohlc/SCMO_<p>_ohlc.csv` + `data/holdings_matrix/price_corrections.csv`; basket files as W1 (newest baskets 2026-09-10/16; none newer exists) |
| Parent | rebuilt from baskets and D18 prices, as T11 | the same rebuild, as T08 |
| Three-index signals (D03) | `extended_2026-10-30/Master/Master_{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}.xlsx` (SC100 rows dated 2011-11-25 or later) | `extended_2026-11-20/Master/Master_{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}.xlsx` (same restriction) |
| MAUc1 signal | D24b `extended_2026-11-12/MAUc1_from_2003/Master_MAUc1.xlsx` | **D24c** `extended_2026-11-20/MAUc1_from_2003/Master_MAUc1.xlsx` |
| GOLDBEES (D09), de-spike range | `analysis/cache/why_gold_ohlc_eikon_extended_2026-11-04.parquet`; range: D24b's daily file, as T11 / T15 | `analysis/cache/why_gold_ohlc_eikon_extended_2026-11-23.parquet`; range D12 (to 2026-09-28; raw OHLC4 after it, as T15) |
| Cash (D11) / R2 | `LBES_Adjusted_Price_data_extended_2026-11-05.csv` / `liquidEtfFinal_extended_2026-11-05.csv` | `LBES_Adjusted_Price_data_extended_2026-11-25.csv` / `liquidEtfFinal_extended_2026-11-25.csv` |
| Index prices | D25 `extended_2026-11-12/index_daily_pre2019/{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}_daily_ohlcv.csv` (`guard_window` with 2014-09-01 for SC100) | **D25d** `extended_2026-11-20/index_daily_2019_2026/{Nifty100,MC100,SC100}_daily_ohlcv.csv` |
| R3 | start 2015-01-02 | live decisions from 2021-11-01 |
| R2 | LIQUIDCASE as cash, whole window | LIQUIDCASE from 2024-01-24 |

**The window end.** 2026-11-20 is the earliest of the roles' last dates (index signals D03, index prices D25d and MAUc1 D24c to 2026-11-20; GOLDBEES D09 to 2026-11-23; cash, stock prices and the published-NAV calendar to 2026-11-25), so it is the latest possible end. The engine asserts it. No draws are made, so no seeds are used.

**Test evidence read by gates only (not data):** `tests/T15/evidence/headline/{w1,w2}/{daily_nav.csv, trades.csv, decisions.csv}`. Not read: D09b, D03b, the tag files D20–D23, D15 AA books, any PENDING or SUPERSEDED row, the superseded or older copies of the W2 files. Reading T15's stored files is a regression gate, not an input to any T16 number.

**Construction, in order.** Steps 1–3, 5, 7–9 and the unchanged parts of 4 and 6 are T15 §3 (and, through it, T14 §3, T11 §3 for W1 and T08 §3 for W2).

1. **Calendar** and **decision dates** per window as above: T0, then the last session of each ISO week after T0; the decision on the last session of the window is made but not traded.
2. **Signals at decision date d.** The latest Master row of each of the three indices and of MAUc1 dated on or before d. IN iff all three SIGN are BUY. g = BUY iff the MAUc1 SIGN is BUY. Regime: IN, OUT-BUY, OUT-SELL as §2.0. B = the indices whose own SIGN is BUY at d (used by `-idx` only; `-all` does not use it).
3. **Targets**: one function `targets(rule, in, g, B)` returns the split parent / GOLDBEES / cash / each index. For the eight T15 rules it returns exactly T15's mapping, so their path is unchanged; for `-all` in OUT-SELL it returns cash 0.25 and each index 0.25. IN: the parent's basket in force at its listed weights renormalised to 1.
4. **Trades.** As §2.2. A trade is due on the next session after decision j (j ≥ 1, a session exists) iff the target vector differs from decision j−1's (for `-all` that is only a change of regime).
5. **No reset inside an unchanged target.**
6. **Parent rebalances.** A basket takes effect on the first session on or after its `availableDate`. While IN the old basket is sold and the new bought at that session's OHLC4. While `e = 0` (including `-all` in OUT-SELL) nothing is traded. While `e = 0.5` (the `-half` comparators) T14's D1 rule.
7. **Initial position** at T0's close, no cost, in every realisation: the target of the decision at T0, with NAV 1 (an IN start holds the basket in force at T0 as drifted since its availableDate; an OUT start holds its sleeve; an OUT-SELL start of `-all` holds 25% of each of the three indices and cash at that day's closes). The two full windows do not start there (W1 starts IN, W2 OUT-BUY), **but both R3 windows do**, so in R3 `-all` starts at 25% each, `-idx` with the B of that day, `-half` as T14, `-liq` all cash.
8. **NAV, statistics:** cash account + Σ units × close (stocks, GOLDBEES, each index); years = (sessions − 1) ÷ 252; CAGR = NAV_end^(1/years) − 1; maximum drawdown, Ulcer index, days ≥ 10% below the running peak, longest time under water, volatility = SD of daily returns × √252, Calmar = CAGR ÷ |maximum drawdown|.
9. **Comparisons** as §2.3, from the stored NAVs; the comparators of §2.4 by the same engine.

**How the test works, in plain words.**

- **The series.** The book is one of the four real parents. Every Friday three weekly index signals and gold's own weekly signal are read. If all three index signals say BUY, the book holds the parent's basket. Otherwise it is in a "sleeve" and the original rule says what the sleeve is: half GOLDBEES and half cash (50/50), or 80% GOLDBEES and 20% cash when gold is BUY and 20/80 when gold is SELL (80/20). T16 changes only the weeks when the three-index signal is OUT and gold is SELL: there the book holds a quarter each of Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100 and the liquid ETF, whatever the indices' own signals say, each index bought at its own average of open, high, low and close with no dividends and no fund cost. Every price and level comes from the approved files of the table above; the 2014-2018 parent is rebuilt from the parent's baskets and stock prices as in T11 (no published NAV exists to check it). *[each series' first and last value printed in §4.0a]*
- **One decision.** On a Friday, look up the latest row of the three index files and of the gold file. Work out the regime (IN, OUT-BUY or OUT-SELL); read off the target for each of the ten rules, and if it differs from last Friday's the trade is on the next session at the average of open, high, low and close. In an OUT-SELL week the `-all` target is the same every week, so it is traded only the Friday the regime starts and the Friday it ends. *[one real row printed in §4.0a: a week where an index is on SELL and `-all` holds it]*
- **The result of one path.** Units of each stock, GOLDBEES, cash and index are fixed between trades; each day the NAV is the sum of units × price; CAGR and drawdown come from that NAV. *[printed in §4.0a]*
- **Entry, drift and exit.** On the session after the regime begins the book sells whatever it held and buys the four lines to a quarter each of its value after cost. Over the following weeks the lines drift with their prices and nothing is traded, even when an index's own signal flips; when the regime ends (the switch turns IN, or gold turns BUY) the four lines are sold and the book moves to the parent or the base sleeve. Each of those two trades costs the usual 10.4 bps on the value traded. *[an entry and an exit worked by hand in §4.0a]*
- **The comparisons.** The new rule's CAGR and worst fall are placed beside the same book's CAGR and worst fall under the original rule, T14's liquid-ETF-only rule, T14's half-parent rule and T15's BUY-indices rule, on the same weeks, prices and costs. No random weeks are drawn, so no percentile or p-value exists; a "pass" means the difference had the stated sign in three of the four books.
- **Leave one spell out and the fund-cost drag.** R4 re-runs the new rule with one OUT-SELL spell held in cash only, to see whether that spell carries the result; R5 re-runs it with half a percentage point a year taken off each index.
- **The comparators.** Holding the parent is what the book would do with no rule; each index alone and the equal-weight three-index basket are what the index leg earned; the constant mix holds the rule's own average shares all the time and shows how much of any gain is just a different average exposure.

**Point-in-time rule.** A decision at d reads Master rows dated at or before d only; a trade is on a session after d. The engine asserts both for every decision, counts them, and writes the counts to `audit.json` (V2). The Master rows were produced afterwards by the production code and are not signals traded at the time, and no MAUc1 row was traded by the desk; disclosed, not corrected.

**Execution and cost.** AGENT.md R1 (next-session OHLC4, price return, 10.4 bps a side, weights drift between rebalances); the first position at T0 is free; no sale at the end; a stock bar without open, high or low is filled at the close; the GOLDBEES fill is T03's de-spike; every regime trade and parent rebalance pays on the value traded, the index lines included. An index is filled at its own OHLC4 from D25 / D25d.

**Effective sample size and power.** 8 OUT-SELL spells per window (7 and 5 in the R3 windows); 228 and 413 weekly decisions; the four books share one market, so they are one sample seen four times. No MDE: no test statistic is computed.

**What the comparisons control for, and what they do not.** Nothing is controlled for chance (no null). They say what each holding earned over the same weeks. In the k = 0 weeks `-all` holds only indices that are on SELL, so C5 is decided partly there; C1 and C4 also reflect that `-all` holds no GOLDBEES and no parent in the regime.

**Known contaminants** (T15's §3 list, plus the extension):

| Contaminant | Handling |
|---|---|
| W1: no published NAV exists before 2019-01-02, so the rebuilt 2014-2018 parent cannot be checked | Disclosed; the rebuilt NAV is written beside the results with a caption saying so |
| W1: nine manual Eikon exports (`data/missing_rics/`, provenance unrecorded, F-AA-D01) supply bars for delisted stocks held in this window | Disclosed (affects the parent and so `-orig`, `-half`, not `-all` in OUT-SELL) |
| Price returns only (dividends not credited on stocks, GOLDBEES, **or the index leg**) | Disclosed. **The index leg is a price index with no dividends and no fund cost, not a tradable instrument**: a real index fund or ETF would differ by roughly the dividend yield minus its costs, and Smallcap 100 / Midcap 100 funds were thin or absent in 2014-2019; R5 tests the cost side only |
| The index prices come from production's Refinitiv file with no second source | Tied to the signals by V3 |
| W1: the session 2017-10-19 (Muhurat evening) is in D26 and has D25 bars but no D18 bars; GOLDBEES has no bar on 2016-10-30 | T11's last-close stand-in and previous-close fill, counted |
| W2: three Budget weekend sessions (2020-02-01, 2025-02-01, 2026-02-01) have no index bar | Last close carried, counted; they are decision sessions only |
| W2: GOLDBEES fills after 2026-09-28 use the raw OHLC4 (no D12 range); the new extension adds more such sessions than T15 had; GOLDBEES has a Muhurat bar on 2026-11-08 that is not a calendar session | As T15; counted in `audit.json`; the non-calendar bar is ignored |
| **The extension (2026-11-04 → 2026-11-20): D03, D25d, D24c and the 2026-11-23 GOLDBEES file were auto-approved on Manu's instruction, not reviewed by him; Postgres `ohlcv_eikon` was rewritten on 2026-11-08, and the D18 extension keeps the approved rows verbatim and appends only the new sessions after a seam check** | Disclosed; the eight T15 rules reproduce T15's W2 to 2026-10-30 (V4(a)); the three new weeks are three weeks of one spell and carry no hold-out |
| The cash file's source before 2026-08-10 is unrecorded (F-AA-D09); the extension runs about 0.5 pp/yr rich against LIQUIDBEES; ~2 days of weekend accrual counted twice (≤ 0.02%) | Disclosed; R2. **Cash is a quarter of `-all`'s regime holding** |
| The rule, its weights, the MAUc1 signal and now the variant were chosen after seeing 2014–2026 results | Disclosed (§2). There is no unseen stretch |
| The four books share one market, one in-or-out series and one gold series, and in OUT-SELL weeks `-all` holds identical lines in all four | Not independent; "3 of 4" is a consistency check |
| Master rows (indices and MAUc1) are a backfill by the production code; MAUc1 is a futures series with roll artifacts | Disclosed |
| `check_approved_data.py` lists `Historical Data/extended_2026-11-12/SOURCE.md` as unregistered (exit code 0) | Not read by this test |
